messages:
maria: Hey team, escalation from customer 'Textly' — embeddings endpoint started returning vectors with the wrong dimension and latency spiked after they enabled batching. They've got requests that used to be 768-dim and now come back 1536-dim. Also per-request latency increased from ~40ms to ~320ms. Can we triage?

alex: Ack. Can you paste the sample request/response and the request_id? Also which model/route are they hitting and any SDK version?

maria: Request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Model: open-redwood-mini-1 (route embeddings-prod). SDK: js-sdk@2.4.1.
Response snippet: 
```json
{"request_id":"req_0a1b2c3d","model":"open-redwood-mini-1","embedding": [0.001, 0.002, ..., 0.003], "dimensions":1536}
```
They assert expected dimensions: 768. Customer turned on client-side batching (batch window 200ms).

jason: Two quick hypotheses: 1) A model variant with double embedding size got rolled into the route (e.g., a larger hidden size variant). 2) Runtime is using a different tokenizer/model mapping that emits pooled features of a concatenated layer. Can you confirm the model version currently pinned for the route?

maria: Pulling from Console shows route embeddings-prod -> open-redwood-mini-1 (no explicit pin, using latest). Last deploy around 1767319000 (yesterday).

ops-bot: Trace captured for req_0a1b2c3d -> trace_id=4a7e9f2b6c (link: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/4a7e9f2b6c)

maria: Pasted the top-level trace spans from the trace UI: 
- route.lookup: 6ms
- auth.check: 2ms
- batching.wait: 220ms (waited for more requests)
- batch.assemble: 4ms
- model.infer: 18ms (per item)
- serialize: 3ms
Total observed client-visible latency: ~260-320ms depending on batch size.

jason: That batching.wait looks like the big diff. If client-side batching is set to 200ms, that adds latency. But that doesn't explain the dimension doubling. For dims: run admin query for model metadata: `rcli models inspect open-redwood-mini-1 --json` and paste the output. If the model artifact changed to a variant with embedding_size=1536 then billing and downstream mismatch are explained.

maria: Ran it, admin output shows embedding_size: 1536 for current artifact id open-redwood-mini-1@v1.7.0. Previous stable v1.4.2 had embedding_size: 768. So looks like a variant bump.

sre-lee: OK. Two actionable items: 1) For latency, advise customer to reduce client batch window (or switch to server-side batching) if they need lower tail latency. 2) For dimension mismatch, we should either pin the route to v1.4.2 or coordinate a migration with the customer so they can adapt. Also add an alert rule on the embeddings route for sudden dimension metric changes.

alex: On the billing side — since billing is per-embedding unit (units = vector_length * count), doubling dims would double their usage/billing for those requests. We should flag billing ops so they can reconcile charges and consider a credits adjustment for the unexpected change.

jason: Suggested mitigation commands: 
```bash
# pin route to previous model version
rcli deployments update --route embeddings-prod --model open-redwood-mini-1@v1.4.2
# temporarily force server-side batching minimal wait
rcli routes update --route embeddings-prod --setting max_batch_ms=10
```
Also plan a controlled rollout for v1.7.0 with a canary percent and explicit dimension metadata exposure in the Console so customers get warned.

maria: I'll propose the pin + credits to Textly and advise reducing the batch window. Also adding a dashboard panel to show 'embedding_size' as a metric per-deployment would have caught this earlier. Can someone add that to observability?

sre-lee: I'll add a Grafana panel and an alert: if embedding_size changes for a route, fire a critical alert. I'll also add a trace breakdown panel that visualizes 'batching.wait' vs 'model.infer' so ops can distinguish batching latency from model compute.

alex: Thanks. I'll file a support billing ticket referencing req_0a1b2c3d and work with billing ops for a credit proposal.

maria: Great. I'll update the customer and close the escalation once the route is pinned and billing case opened. cc @jason @sre-lee :thumbsup:
